SEC Must Block Anthropic IPO Over Financial Opacity
Huge spending commitments mask tepid model reception and balance sheet risks.

Anthropic is preparing for an IPO while facing significant financial opacity. The company has committed to 15 GW of data center capacity but estimates it will ultimately need 20-25 GW. Its latest Fable 5 model received a tepid commercial response. Investors need clarity on who bears the cost of these massive infrastructure bets before buying shares. The SEC must ensure public protection against unverified liabilities.

OpenAI Retires ChatGPT Classic App in 2027
The old app is leaving. The new one is coming.

OpenAI has announced that the standalone ChatGPT Classic app will be retired on January 30, 2027. Users opening the app now see a banner confirming this date. The company plans to combine the Chat and Work tabs into a single new application. Codex will remain a separate experience within the ChatGPT desktop app. This consolidation marks a significant shift in how users access OpenAI's core services, moving away from distinct mobile applications toward a unified ecosystem. The change affects millions of daily users who rely on the classic interface for quick interactions.

Anthropic Blocks Game Modding Ahead of Mega IPO
Claude AI restricts reverse engineering. The cost of safety is rising.

Anthropic has quietly updated Claude to block video game modding and reverse engineering, a move reported by Tom's Hardware. This restriction impacts projects like browser ports of World of Warcraft and Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. The decision comes as the company prepares for a major initial public offering. While safety is the stated goal, the practical effect is the loss of community-driven preservation and modification tools. Investors must weigh ethical guardrails against the utility of open-ended AI applications in creative and technical fields.

Sam Altman meets Samsung execs in Yongin, building on chip partnerships.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman visited South Korea again, this time meeting with roughly 50 executives from Samsung affiliates. The visit underscores OpenAI's strategy to secure hardware partnerships as it expands its AI infrastructure globally. While no specific deals were announced, the high-level engagement signals continued alignment between the tech giants. Anthropic Blocks Claude From Recreating Video Games
Claude now refuses to generate recreations of existing games, following legal pressure.

Anthropic has updated Claude to prevent users from generating AI recreations of their favorite video games. This restriction follows a $1.5 billion settlement with authors and an Elvis Presley estate lawsuit. The change limits creative tools but avoids new litigation risks. Users can still build original content, but cannot replicate protected works directly through the model.

Anthropic restricts Claude Code from remaking video games
A rule update stops the AI tool from recreating existing titles.

An update to Anthropic’s Claude Code pushed on October 27 introduces new rules that appear to prohibit the tool from remaking video games. The change was identified by Chasm, a writer for Game Developer who has credited work on titles like Endless Space 2 and Zephon. While the specific text of the rules remains internal, the restriction signals a shift in how AI coding assistants might handle intellectual property concerns during the generation process. This move addresses potential legal risks but may limit the tool's utility for developers looking to iterate on legacy codebases or create retro-style projects without manual intervention.

OpenAI cuts funding target to $20B, down from $30B
Valuation drops as OpenAI scales back fundraising goals ahead of IPO.

The Financial Times reports that OpenAI has reduced its latest funding target to $20 billion, a significant decrease from the previously reported $30 billion goal. This adjustment comes alongside a valuation shift, with earlier targets sitting at $1.4 trillion and subsequently $1.25 trillion before an anticipated initial public offering. The company is now exploring a retail offering for wealthy individuals to help reach this new capital threshold. While the first close is expected to be even lower than the $20 billion figure, the strategic pivot signals a recalibration of investor expectations in the high-stakes artificial intelligence market.
